title: The Bookkeeper Who Found the Silver Was Light — Then Fell Down Shaft Three
description:
In 1878, Cerro Gordo was one of the richest silver-lead mines in the American West, shipping over $500,000 in bullion in a single year. Bookkeeper Louis D. Gordon logged every 83-pound bar hauled down the Yellow Grade Road — until he noticed something wrong. For fourteen months, bars were coming up two pounds light. Sixty bars. Roughly $18,000 in stolen silver.

On March 2nd, 1878, Gordon wrote to the mine's owners demanding a full audit. Two weeks later he was found dead at the bottom of Shaft Number Three, his neck broken and his ledger missing. The coroner ruled it an accidental fall the same day — no autopsy, case closed within the hour. Shipments quietly returned to full weight within a month.

No one was ever charged. The record office burned in 1880, destroying what books remained. The $18,000 was never recovered, and Gordon's ledger has never been found. Subscribe now 👇
